items.title: Clayton Duerr Interview, 1972-04-17
items.q: What about when he was with Goodman? Was Goodman making any money there?

ctx.x: Was he a big name? He was a big name around New York. He could have got much further than he, although he did all right I guess, but I mean he got to be pretty well known around New York school, I tell you. He was a good piano player at that time. When we used to go up to Harlem there used to be a lot of guys who would go up to hear him play, I tell you that. Johnny Green used to go up and listen to him play. And a lot of other piano players, Eddie Bushkin used to go up and listen to him all the time and cook.…
it. What about when he was with Goodman? Was Goodman making any money there?
Well, he didn't make money. You know at that time I thought of it as a deal was. I don't know exactly what it was. I guess it was good for that time. He didn't stay with Goodman too
